catalog_quote: ... Hauptakzent noch ein Nebenakzent zu beachten. Der Hauptakzent [§ 204] wird mit dem Akut, der Nebenakzent mit dem Gravis bezeichnet. Die Hauptregeln für die Setzung des Akzentes scheinen folgende zu sein: 1. Der Hauptakzent liegt auf der Stammsilbe, wenn diese gedehnt oder der Stamm dreisilbig ist. 2. Bei einsilbigen Stämmen rückt der Akzent auf die vorangehende Präfixsilbe, desgleichen bei zweisilbigen Stämmen ohne gelängten Vokal. 3. Im letzteren Falle hat er sogar die Neigung auf die erste Präfixsilbe überzugehen. 4. Bei mehr als viersilbigen Wörtern liegt der Akzent auf der vorletzten Silbe. Zu 1. umugu nda, 3 Garten, Feld; umwäha, 3 Zeit von einer Regenperiode zur anderen, Jahr; umwo tho, 3 Feuer; umunu'nsi, 3 Gestank; umuvömbi, 1 Arbeiter ... [p. 80, § 209, verbs] ... Stammsilbe, wenn diese gedehnt oder wenn das Verb dreisilbig ist. 2. Bei einsilbigen Verben rückt der Akzent auf die vorhergehende Präfixsilbe, desgleichen bei zweisilbigen ohne gelängten Vokal. 3. Bei erweiterten Verbalverbindungen: Wird ein Obj. Pron ... [p. 81] ... 5. Tritt an einfache Verbalverbindungen und an kausativ und passiv gebrauchte Verben ein Suffix, so wird der Akzent auf die vorletzte Silbe gelegt, die dann auch Hochton hat ... [p. 83, § 212] ... 3. Alle anderen Verben haben ihn auf der drittletzten Silbe. Dabei hat die Silbe, die den Akzent trägt, einen steigenden Ton.

new_statements.translation: ... besides the main accent a secondary accent must also be noted. The main accent is marked with the acute, the secondary accent with the grave. The main rules for the placement of the accent seem to be the following: 1. The main accent lies on the stem syllable if it is lengthened or the stem is trisyllabic. 2. With monosyllabic stems the accent moves onto the preceding prefix syllable, likewise with disyllabic stems without a lengthened vowel. 3. In the latter case it even tends to pass onto the first prefix syllable. 4. In words of more than four syllables the accent lies on the penultimate syllable. [p. 80 par. 209, verbs: '(accent on the) stem syllable if it is lengthened or the verb is trisyllabic; with monosyllabic verbs the accent moves to the preceding prefix syllable, likewise with disyllabic ones without a lengthened vowel'; p. 83: 'All other verbs have it on the antepenultimate syllable. The syllable bearing the accent then has a rising tone.']

new_statements.rule_in_words: Busse treats Nyiha as having both lexical/grammatical 'musical tone' (H, L, two mids, rising, falling; par. 201-203) and a dynamic accent (Hauptakzent + Nebenakzent; par. 204-213) whose position is fixed by morphology, vowel length and word length rather than lexically: in nouns and simple verbs the main accent sits on the stem(-initial) syllable when that syllable is long (incl. pre-NC lengthening: umugúnda, umuvómbi) or the stem has three syllables; with monosyllabic stems and short disyllabic stems it retracts onto the prefix syllable (even the first prefix syllable); words over four syllables take penult accent. In extended verb forms the accent moves with the morphology (object prefix or derivational suffix -> penult with H; some TAM forms final syllable with H; subjunctive antepenult with rising tone). Net effect: prominence falls on the antepenult or on a heavy penult counted from the word end, and the accented syllable normally carries H or rising tone. Yukawa 1989 (tone-only study, Mbeya speaker) independently finds H on the word-antepenult in most infinitives, a falling-toned penult for NC-final stems and H on the penult of causatives/passives, i.e. the same placements analysed as tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Busse marks a Nebenakzent (grave): on the first syllable of certain derived nouns that keep main accent elsewhere (p. 80), on the negative particle -tha- and on the tense particle -a- ('Nebenakzent mit Hochton', p. 82); in negated four-syllable subjunctives -tha- and the penult both get an accent, 'wenn ich recht gehört habe, sind beide Akzente gleich stark' (p. 83).
new_statements.exceptions: Rule 4 (words of more than four syllables -> penult); nouns with wa-/ha- prefixes seem to accent the prefix (p. 80); some noun/verb forms have final-syllable accent with H while the penult is L (pp. 80-81); exceptions in simple forms of monosyllabic and short disyllabic stems and in the 'Undeterminiertes Futurum' (p. 81, points 8-9). Busse hedges throughout ('scheinen', 'wenn ich recht gehört habe') and states in the Vorwort (p. 7) that a full statement of the accent laws and an investigation of the relation between tone and accent could not be carried out because the war ended the fieldwork early.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level citation forms; separate rule sets for nouns (par. 204-208), verb forms by TAM/derivation (par. 209-212) and possessive pronouns (par. 213). Accent interacts with tone (accented syllable H or rising) and with vowel length (long and pre-NC vowels attract it); Yukawa 1989 reports that in present-day Mbeya Nyiha the old long vowels have shortened. Variety: Nyiha of Mbozi (Moravian mission area), SW Tanzania, fieldwork 1930s-1956.
new_statements.identity_note: Busse 1960 describes the Nyiha of Mbozi (Moravian mission field, SW Tanzania; Guthrie M23) = Glottolog nyih1240 'Nyiha (Tanzania)' [nih], not Nyiha of Malawi [nyr] or Nyika [nkv/nkt]. Yukawa 1989's speaker is from near Mbeya (self-designation ishinyiha), same language; Yukawa notes his variety has lost the vowel-length contrast that Busse marks, and that a length-preserving dialect may exist nearby. Kashoki 1978's 'Nyiha' is the Zambian (Isoka) variety and gives no Nyiha-specific prosodic statement.
